metrics.name: Offered demand
metrics.formula: Σ external arrivals + upstream calls × routing × bounded retry factor
assumptions: Downstream offered demand is propagated independently of admission limits.
Analytical offered-load model. Finite queues, bursts, joins and timeouts require the discrete-event engine.
Illustrative test inputs.
Analytical rates exclude additional time-varying burst intervals. Inspect the simulation for transient demand and recovery.

metrics.name: Service-slot utilization

metrics.name: Mean queue wait
metrics.formula: Erlang-C × mean service time / (servers × (1 − utilization))
assumptions: M/M/c: Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service, FCFS, infinite buffer, stationary load.
Analytical offered-load model. Finite queues, bursts, joins and timeouts require the discrete-event engine.
Illustrative test inputs.
Analytical rates exclude additional time-varying burst intervals. Inspect the simulation for transient demand and recovery.
limitations: Transformed downstream arrivals may violate independence; validate using simulation.

metrics.name: Maximum observed foreground latency
metrics.formula: maximum duration among completed observed foreground requests
assumptions: Illustrative test inputs.
Declared service slots model local processing contention; slots release before downstream dependencies.
Random failures use declared independent probabilities. Timeouts do not cancel downstream work.
Intervals describe simulation sampling uncertainty, not accuracy of the supplied model.
When CPU demand is separately declared, CPU centers execute first and non-CPU delay follows. Declared memory is reserved during local processing, including CPU wait.
limitations: Right-censored, failed and dropped requests prevent a positive strict-deadline assessment.

limitations: Transformed downstream arrivals may violate independence; validate using simulation.

metrics.name: Offered demand
metrics.formula: Σ external arrivals + upstream calls × routing × bounded retry factor
assumptions: Downstream offered demand is propagated independently of admission limits.
Analytical offered-load model. Finite queues, bursts, joins and timeouts require the discrete-event engine.
Illustrative test inputs.
Analytical rates exclude additional time-varying burst intervals. Inspect the simulation for transient demand and recovery.

metrics.name: Service-slot utilization
metrics.formula: offered rate × mean service seconds / service slots
assumptions: illustrative input; not measured production performance.
Analytical offered-load model. Finite queues, bursts, joins and timeouts require the discrete-event engine.
Illustrative test inputs.
Analytical rates exclude additional time-varying burst intervals. Inspect the simulation for transient demand and recovery.
limitations: Service-slot utilization is not CPU utilization.

metrics.name: Mean queue wait
metrics.formula: Erlang-C × mean service time / (servers × (1 − utilization))
assumptions: M/M/c: Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service, FCFS, infinite buffer, stationary load.
Analytical offered-load model. Finite queues, bursts, joins and timeouts require the discrete-event engine.
Illustrative test inputs.
Analytical rates exclude additional time-varying burst intervals. Inspect the simulation for transient demand and recovery.
limitations: Transformed downstream arrivals may violate independence; validate using simulation.

limitations: Local latency excludes downstream dependencies; end-to-end latency requires simulation.
